title: Raising the Aspirations of Those Who Are Better Than They Think
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article focuses on colleagues who underestimate their own talent and potential, and the leadership work required to raise their sights. The author describes how these team members need to hear, in vivid and specific terms, why a leader believes in them and what they're capable of achieving, since self-doubt rarely dissolves on its own. Backed by genuine investment in growth opportunities, this kind of encouragement can produce what the piece calls an 'internal eruption,' unlocking ambitions the person had suppressed. The article closes with a well-known quote about aiming too low, framing this as a leader's responsibility to actively address.
points: Some talented team members underestimate their own potential and need a push to aim higher.
Vivid, specific encouragement from a respected leader can help people overcome self-limiting beliefs.
Pairing encouragement with real growth opportunities makes the message credible, not empty.
Raising a colleague's aspirations can have a life-altering impact on their trajectory.
Leaders bear responsibility for identifying and challenging those who are selling themselves short.
quotes: Some team members and colleagues are better than they think they are.
Good leaders don’t accept the low bar these team members have placed on themselves.
The best leaders describe in vivid detail who they see in front of them, why they believe in this person’s talents, and what success they expect this individual to achieve.
Leaders who work to raise the aspirations of valued colleagues can have a life-altering impact on their future.
In the words of a consummate performer and artist, “The greatest danger for most of us is not that our aim is too high and we miss it, but that it is too low and we reach it.
Leaders show people the stars and ask them to dream even higher.
